subject: Chemistry
description: Carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, nucleic acids: structure + function

questions.explanation: PROTEINS are POLYMERS of AMINO ACIDS, joined by PEPTIDE BONDS (−CO−NH−). 20 standard amino acids; humans need 9 ESSENTIAL ones from diet (rest body can synthesise). Each amino acid: −NH₂ + −COOH + R-group (side chain) on a central carbon. PROTEIN STRUCTURE 4 levels: PRIMARY (amino acid sequence), SECONDARY (alpha-helix, beta-sheet — H-bonding patterns), TERTIARY (3D folding via various bonds), QUATERNARY (multiple sub-units, e.g., Hb has 4). INSIGHT — proteins do EVERYTHING: enzymes (catalysts), structural (collagen, keratin), transport (Hb), antibodies (immune), hormones (insulin), receptors. RELATED: carbs polymerise glucose; nucleic acids polymerise nucleotides; lipids aren't true polymers.

questions.explanation: GLUCOSE: C₆H₁₂O₆ — HEXOSE (6-C) sugar; primary energy source for cells. Same formula as FRUCTOSE (fruit sugar) + GALACTOSE — these are STRUCTURAL ISOMERS (same molecular formula, different structures). DISACCHARIDES (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁): SUCROSE = glucose + fructose (table sugar); LACTOSE = glucose + galactose (milk sugar; some adults are lactose-intolerant — lack the enzyme lactase); MALTOSE = glucose + glucose. POLYSACCHARIDES: STARCH (plant storage), GLYCOGEN (animal storage in liver + muscles), CELLULOSE (plant cell walls — humans CAN'T digest because no enzyme cellulase; ruminants can via gut bacteria).

questions.explanation: NUCLEIC ACIDS (DNA + RNA) are POLYMERS of NUCLEOTIDES. Each nucleotide = (1) PENTOSE SUGAR (deoxyribose for DNA; ribose for RNA); (2) PHOSPHATE group; (3) NITROGENOUS BASE — A, T, G, C in DNA (T replaced by U in RNA). Nucleotides linked by PHOSPHODIESTER bonds → backbone. Two strands of DNA pair via H-bonds: A=T (2 H-bonds), G≡C (3 H-bonds). 'CHARGAFF'S RULE': %A = %T, %G = %C in DNA. Watson + Crick (1953) discovered double-helix structure (with Rosalind Franklin's X-ray data — Photo 51). Nobel 1962. Human DNA: ~3 billion bp; 23 chromosome pairs.

questions.explanation: TRIGLYCERIDES = GLYCEROL (3-OH alcohol) + 3 FATTY ACIDS, linked by ester bonds. SATURATED fatty acids (no C=C) → solid at room temp (animal fats — butter, ghee). UNSATURATED (1+ C=C) → liquid (vegetable oils — olive, sunflower). HYDROGENATION turns oils into solid fats (vanaspati ghee) — but creates TRANS FATS (linked to heart disease). OMEGA-3 / 6 / 9 FATS = unsaturated, named by position of first double bond. CHOLESTEROL — different class (a STEROL, not glyceride; component of cell membranes; precursor of bile salts + sex hormones + Vit D). HDL = 'good' cholesterol; LDL = 'bad'.

questions.explanation: ENZYMES — usually PROTEINS (some are RNA — ribozymes — discovered later; expanded definition). Function: speed up biochemical reactions by lowering activation energy. SPECIFIC: each enzyme acts on a specific SUBSTRATE (lock-and-key model; or induced-fit). Affected by: pH, temperature (DENATURATION at high temp); inhibitors. Examples: AMYLASE (saliva — breaks starch), PEPSIN (stomach acid — proteins), TRYPSIN (small intestine — proteins), LIPASE (fats), LACTASE (lactose). NAMES often end in '-ASE'. INSIGHT — without enzymes, life would be too slow; some reactions take seconds with enzymes vs years without.

questions.stem: Which biomolecule provides the MOST energy per gram (~9 kcal/g)?
questions.explanation: ENERGY DENSITY: FATS ~9 kcal/g (highest); CARBS ~4 kcal/g; PROTEINS ~4 kcal/g; ALCOHOL ~7 kcal/g. WHY fats give more energy: more reduced (more C-H bonds, less oxidised) → more energy released on oxidation. EVOLUTIONARY: fats are concentrated energy storage — animals store excess as fat. WATER content also matters: fats anhydrous (no water) → very compact storage. Glycogen in muscles/liver is stored WITH water → less energy-dense in body. Vitamins + minerals: NO calories themselves, but ENABLE other reactions. INSIGHT — daily Indian dietary need ~2000-2500 kcal; obesity = excess fat storage from chronic surplus calories.

questions.stem: VITAMIN C (Ascorbic acid) is also a:
questions.explanation: VITAMIN C = ASCORBIC ACID. WATER-SOLUBLE (along with B-complex). ANTIOXIDANT (neutralises free radicals). Helps: collagen synthesis (skin, blood vessels, bones), iron absorption, immunity, wound healing. DEFICIENCY → SCURVY (bleeding gums, weakness, joint pain — historically killed many sailors before fresh fruit/limes became standard). RDA ~75 mg/day (more for smokers). SOURCES: amla, citrus, guava, capsicum, kiwi, berries, leafy greens. Cooking destroys ~20-50% (heat-sensitive). VITAMINS classification: WATER-SOLUBLE (B + C, excreted excess in urine, daily need); FAT-SOLUBLE (A, D, E, K — stored in liver/fat, can accumulate to toxic levels).
